introduction: ERC-681 defines a URL format that encodes Ethereum transaction requests, especially payment requests in ether and ERC-20 tokens, so they can be embedded in QR codes, hyperlinks, emails, or chat messages. It was proposed by Daniel A. Nagy in August 2017. A request uses the ethereum: scheme followed by a target address, an optional chain ID, an optional function name, and query parameters such as value, gas, and ABI-typed arguments. Opening the URL launches the user's wallet with a pre-filled transaction to confirm.
designPurpose: ERC-681 was designed to bring the convenience of Bitcoin-style payment URLs to Ethereum. Before it there was no standard way to hand a fully parameterized transaction to a wallet, so senders copied addresses and amounts by hand, inviting errors and phishing. By standardizing an ethereum: URL with a target address, optional chain ID, function name, and typed parameters, ERC-681 lets any channel deliver a request that a wallet can parse and present for confirmation, while leaving every amount editable by the user.
commonUsage: Payment-request URLs are used by wallets, point-of-sale systems, and donation pages that render an ethereum: link or QR code for a specific address and amount. The native-token form requests ether through a value parameter, while the token form targets an ERC-20 contract's transfer function with address and uint256 arguments. ENS names resolved through ERC-137 may stand in for hexadecimal addresses, though clients give raw 0x addresses precedence to reduce phishing risk.
sim.paymentRequestWalkthrough.name: Payment Request Walkthrough
sim.paymentRequestWalkthrough.desc: Follow a payment request from an ethereum: URL through the payer's wallet to a signed transaction.
sim.paymentRequestWalkthrough.step.build: The payee chooses a beneficiary address and an amount to request payment for.
sim.paymentRequestWalkthrough.step.encod: The address, chain ID, and value are encoded into an ethereum: URL that can be shown as a QR code or hyperlink.
sim.paymentRequestWalkthrough.step.scan: The payer scans or opens the link; the wallet parses the URL and presents a pre-filled, editable transaction for confirmation.
sim.paymentRequestWalkthrough.step.send: After the payer confirms, the wallet signs and broadcasts a transaction sending the requested value to the target address.
